title: How to Evaluate a Position
description: Judge any position using four pillars: material, king safety, pawn structure, and piece activity. A clear evaluation tells you whether to attack, defend, or simplify.

sections.title: The Four Pillars
sections.content: Evaluate every position by asking four questions: Who has more material? Whose king is safer? Who has the better pawn structure? Whose pieces are more active? The answers point you to the right plan.

positions.commentary: A balanced position. Material is equal, both kings are castled, structures are sound. The battle will be decided by who activates their pieces better.

sections.title: From Evaluation to Plan
sections.content: Your evaluation dictates your strategy. If you are better, increase the pressure and avoid simplifying into nothing. If you are worse, seek activity or simplify toward a draw. If equal, improve your worst-placed piece.

positions.commentary: When unsure what to do, improve your worst-placed piece. This simple rule turns a vague position into a concrete plan.
hints: Let the evaluation guide the plan

exercises.title: Improve a Piece
exercises.description: White to play. Activate the least useful rook by bringing it toward an open or soon-to-open file.
hints: A rook belongs on a central file
